At constant speed up the slope, driving force balances resistance plus the component of weight: $F_D = R + mg\sin\theta$.
Substitute $R = 1250\text{ N}$ and $mg = 14000\text{ N}$ to find $\sin\theta$, then calculate $\theta = \arcsin(\sin\theta)$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the driving force from power $64\text{ kW} = 64000\text{ W}$ and speed $32\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{64000}{32} = 2000\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces parallel to the incline for constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$F_D - R - mg\sin\theta = 0$$
$$2000 - 1250 - 1400(10)\sin\theta = 0$$
$$750 = 14000\sin\theta$$

ai_rubric.Using Power and Resistance Relationships: Sets up $64000/32 = 1250 + 14000\sin\theta$ and solves to obtain $\theta = 3.1^\circ$.

teacher_walkthrough:
State the relationship connecting driving force, power, and speed:
$$P = F_D v$$
Substitute $P = 64\text{ kW} = 64000\text{ W}$ and constant speed $v = 32\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$64000 = F_D (32)$$
$$F_D = \frac{64000}{32} = 2000\text{ N}$$

Identify the forces acting on the car parallel to the inclined road:
- Forward driving force up the slope: $F_D = 2000\text{ N}$
- Constant resistance opposing motion down the slope: $R = 1250\text{ N}$
- Downward component of weight along the slope: $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\theta = (1400)(10)\sin\theta = 14000\sin\theta$

Because the speed is constant, the acceleration is zero ($a = 0$). Equate the forward force to the total retarding force:
$$F_D = R + mg\sin\theta$$
$$2000 = 1250 + 14000\sin\theta$$
Subtract $1250$ from both sides:
$$750 = 14000\sin\theta$$
Divide both sides by $14000$:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{750}{14000} = \frac{75}{1400} = \frac{3}{56} \approx 0.0535714$$

Take the inverse sine:
$$\theta = \arcsin(0.0535714) \approx 3.0708^\circ$$
Rounding to one decimal place gives:
$$\theta = 3.1^\circ$$
Thus the angle of inclination of the road is $3.1^\circ$.
